items.title: Netanyahu condemns violence in West Bank
items.standfirst: It was a rare condemnation from what is widely seen as the most religious and ultranationalist government in Israel’s history. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned recent attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, but described the violence as the actions of a “handful of rioters.” Tensions have surged across the territory, with activists accusing settlers of acting with impunity. Much of the recent violence has taken place in the town of Qusra. Peter O’Brien reports.

items.title: Death toll rises as 3,000 remain missing in Nepal, China
items.standfirst: Rescue and relief efforts in Nepal and Tibet have been hampered this Sunday by heavy rain and rising river levels. The latest figures following Wednesday’s flash floods put the death toll at 750, while more than 3,000 people remain missing. Nepal’s disaster authorities are urging rescue teams to “exercise caution”, warning that bad weather, swollen rivers and the threat of further flooding could hamper operations. Shazab Wahlah reports from the town of Bidur.

items.title: Nepal-Tibet floods live: At least 750 dead as rising water levels hamper rescue efforts

Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

items.title: NASA set to launch Roman telescope to provide 'a new atlas of the universe'
items.standfirst: NASA is preparing to launch its Roman Space Telescope on Sunday aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket, beginning a multi-year mission to create a vast new map of the cosmos. With a field of view far wider than Hubble’s, Roman will search for exoplanets and supernovae while also probing two of the biggest mysteries in physics: dark matter and dark energy.

items.title: Ontario’s Doug Ford prods Trump with sign rejecting ‘Lake America’ name
items.standfirst: The 'Lake Ontario' sign comes in response to the US president's efforts to rename the body of water 'Lake America'.
items.content: The 'Lake Ontario' sign comes in response to the US president's efforts to rename the body of water 'Lake America'.

items.title: Ontario premier slams Trump's order: "It's Lake Ontario now and forever"
items.standfirst: Amid an ongoing trade war​ between Canada and the United States, President Trump last week sought to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" by executive order.
items.content: Amid an ongoing trade war​ between Canada and the United States, President Trump last week sought to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" by executive order.
